quickAnswer: Natick pairs expensive homes (median value $710,100, ACS 2022) with a lot of shared buildings: 39.6% of homes are in multi-unit buildings, 5th highest of 50 towns. Shared buildings often raise questions about equipment placement and building rules.
body: ## Valuable houses, shared walls

Natick's median owner-occupied home is worth $710,100 in the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), 13th highest of the 50 towns we serve and well above the $579,150 of the middle town. Yet the town is not made of large detached houses alone. Multi-unit buildings hold 6,332 of 16,003 housing units, 39.6% and 5th highest, while detached single-family houses are 9,063 units (56.6%), 41st of 50. Buildings of 5 or more units hold 4,321 homes (27.0%), two-family buildings 1,232 (7.7%), three- and four-unit buildings 779 (4.9%), and townhouse-style units 606 (3.8%).

For a homeowner, a median value of $710,100 makes any equipment choice a sizable one. For a condo owner or a landlord, the building often limits what is possible, and the assessment of the home's heating load comes before the quote.
## Renters, electric heat and a population of 36,589

Natick has 36,589 residents, fourth largest of the 50 towns. Renters live in 4,978 of 15,568 occupied households (32.0%), sixth highest, against 16.4% for the middle town. Electricity is the main heating source in 3,202 homes (20.6%), also sixth highest, while utility gas serves 8,033 (51.6%), fuel oil or kerosene 3,787 (24.3%) and bottled gas 462 (3.0%).

Electric heat in a rental often means the tenant pays the meter, which makes efficiency a tenant concern as well as a landlord one. For oil households the options are a new boiler, a gas conversion where a main runs, or a heat pump. If heat fails in a rental, 105 CMR 410.201 sets the floor: 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight, for the length of the heating season. Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord pays. This is general information, not legal advice.
## The 1874 fire, the shoe boom and the housing stock

Natick was a farming town until the sewing machine arrived in 1858 and shoe factories followed. By 1880 it had 23 operating factories and ranked third in the nation for shoe production. In 1874 a fire in downtown Natick destroyed 18 business blocks, two shoe factories, the Town Hall, the only fire engine house and the Congregational Church, along with many private homes. The new Central Fire Station on Summer Street was completed in 1875.

The census age bands show the stock today. Units dating from 1939 or earlier number 3,260 (20.4%), 14th highest, and 3,810 (23.8%) went up from 1940 to 1959. Another 2,739 (17.1%) are from 1960 to 1979, and 3,537 (22.1%) from 1980 to 1999. Newer construction is not rare: 2,657 units (16.6%) are from 2000 or later and 1,418 (8.9%) since 2010. Overall, 9,809 units (61.3%) predate 1980 and the median home dates to 1966.

The H. Harwood & Sons baseball factory, described in the town's history as the world's first plant for making baseballs, was converted to condominiums in 1988. Converted factories like that can have thick walls, tall rooms and little space for equipment.
## Natick's neighborhoods

- **Natick Center:** the civic and cultural hub, with municipal buildings, historic buildings and churches, plus the state-designated cultural district named in 2012.
- **South Natick:** where the town began on the Charles River. Housing developers who lived there avoided building major tract neighborhoods in this part of town.
- **East and West Natick:** retail along Route 9 and the Natick Mall area, bordering Wellesley and Framingham.
Lake Cochituate and Dug Pond account for 7.04% of the town's area.
## Which utility, which rebate

Which supplier serves each Natick address is not something we have confirmed, so we name none. Your electric bill settles it, and the answer sets the rebate route. The [heat pump page](/cities/natick/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers what that means for the town's housing.

faq.q: Why do so many Natick homes share walls?
faq.a: Census figures show 39.6% of Natick homes are in multi-unit buildings, 5th highest of the 50 towns we serve. That mixes condos, apartments and two-family houses with the detached houses. For equipment, it means placement, association rules and shared systems are often the first questions.

faq.q: Is a heat pump worth considering in Natick?
faq.a: Often, especially for the 20.6% of homes with electric heat or for oil homes. A heat pump heats and cools, and it needs a correctly sized design. Rebates depend on the utility serving your address, so check before you buy. We size from a heating-load assessment.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in a Natick rental?
faq.a: The landlord, unless the lease says otherwise. With 32.0% of households renting, sixth highest of the 50 towns, tenants should report an outage in writing and keep a copy. The temperature minimums are in the renters section above. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: How old are Natick's homes, and does it matter for a new system?
faq.a: The median home dates to 1966, and 9,809 of 16,003 units (61.3%) predate 1980. Yet 2,657 units are from 2000 or later. Age matters for insulation, air leaks and old piping, so a house from the 1940 to 1959 band and a condo from 2000 or later need different sizing.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Gas heats 51.6% of Natick homes and oil 24.3%, and 39.6% of homes sit in shared buildings. We plan replacements around the building and the permit.
body: ## Replacing heat when the building sets the rules

A heating replacement in Natick starts with a question about the building. A detached house usually gives you more freedom of fuel and equipment. A condo or apartment building may have a shared boiler, a rule about where flues may exit and a board that has to agree. We ask about all of it at the estimate.
### Gas, oil and electric

Gas is the most common heating fuel, with 8,033 homes, oil next at 3,787 and electricity third at 3,202. A gas furnace swap is usually a quick job. An oil boiler replacement involves the tank, flue and chimney. A home with electric baseboard has no central equipment, so the question can be whether to add a heat pump.
### Older downtown buildings

Natick Center has historic buildings and churches alongside newer municipal buildings, and older buildings there may carry radiators, tall ceilings and deep basements. The town counts 3,260 units from 1939 or earlier. A boiler swap in one depends on the piping and the radiators, not just the size of the unit. We inspect first.
### Multi-family buildings

Natick has 1,232 units in two-family buildings, 779 in buildings of 3 or 4 units and 4,321 in buildings of five or more. Where one boiler feeds several households, the board or landlord has to be part of the plan, and the work gets scheduled around the days the building can be without heat.
### High-value homes

With a median owner-occupied value of $710,100, a replacement is worth doing carefully. We prefer to put the options on paper: a like-for-like swap, a higher-efficiency unit, or a change of fuel. The written estimate lists each.
### Gas permits

A new gas furnace or boiler brings in a licensed plumber or gas fitter, who pulls the permit, and an inspection follows the install. Venting, gas piping and combustion air are the usual points of attention.
### Rentals

Landlords must keep rental units warm in the heating season, so a failed boiler in a multi-family house is an urgent call. With 4,978 renter households, that case is not rare here. See the state rules in our [city overview](/cities/natick).
### Emergencies
No heat? Call (508) 786-8755, any hour.

faq.q: Can I replace a condo's boiler without the association?
faq.a: Usually not if the boiler is common equipment. Check your documents and bring the board in early. Natick has 6,332 units in multi-unit buildings, so shared systems are common, and a board that is consulted before the estimate tends to move faster afterward.

faq.q: Should I convert from oil to gas in Natick?
faq.a: It depends on whether a main reaches your street and on the connection cost. About 24.3% of Natick homes burn oil, and a heat pump or a new oil boiler may suit some of them better. We lay the three routes side by side in writing.

faq.q: My Natick house was built between 1940 and 1959. Will a new boiler need new piping?
faq.a: Possibly, in part. The town has 3,810 units from 1940 to 1959, and houses of that age can have older pipe runs, radiators and chimney liners. We look at those before choosing a size, since an old system can hide leaks that a new boiler would expose.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Natick's mix of detached houses, townhouses, condos and apartments means cooling is rarely one-size-fits-all. Outdoor unit placement and building rules often matter as much as the equipment.
body: ## Cooling in a town of condos and large houses

Detached houses are 56.6% of Natick's homes, and a large minority share walls. Each cools differently. Detached houses can often take central air if ducts are sound. Attached homes and apartments need a placement plan.
### Detached houses

In a house with forced-air heat, a cooling coil can often share the ducts if they carry enough air. Houses heated with radiators have no ducts, and a ductless mini-split cools without them. For a ducted system we check duct size, return air and the blower first. Many older homes were built without central air, and Natick's median home dates to 1966, so adding it later may be the real question. Two-family houses (1,232 units) and buildings of 3 or 4 units (779) can sometimes take a separate ductless system on each floor.
### Condos and apartments

Association rules often decide where an outdoor unit can sit and how line sets run. We can propose a layout to bring to the board. In a rental building, any new unit also needs the landlord's consent.
### Converted buildings

Converted factories, such as the baseball factory made into condominiums in 1988, can have thick walls and unusual layouts. Equipment placement there can be a design problem, and ductless may solve it.
### Newer buildings

Natick has 2,657 units from 2000 or later (16.6%), including 1,418 from 2010 on. Newer buildings are more likely to have ducts laid out with cooling in mind, so the question is often a coil or a condenser, not a whole new duct system.
### What the ranks say

Natick is 41st of 50 for detached houses and 5th for shared buildings. In that mix, cooling is often decided jointly by owners, associations and landlords. A median home value of $710,100 also puts the town 13th, so owners tend to weigh equipment choices with care.
### Electricity

Electricity is already the main heating source in 3,202 Natick homes (20.6%). For those households a heat pump can do the cooling and the heating from one set of equipment. See the [heat pump page](/cities/natick/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Diagnosis first
We diagnose before suggesting replacement, since the fault is not always a dead unit.

faq.q: What cooling works for an older Natick house with radiators?
faq.a: A ductless mini-split is often the practical choice because it needs no ducts and only a small wall opening. The number of indoor heads depends on the layout, and a heat pump version can also supply heat on shoulder-season days.

faq.q: Will my condo association allow an outdoor unit?
faq.a: It depends on its rules. We check clearance and drainage and propose a placement you can bring to the board. Natick has 4,321 units in buildings of five or more, so many owners go through this approval step.

faq.q: Can a two-family house in Natick cool each floor separately?
faq.a: Often, yes. A ductless system can put an outdoor unit and indoor heads on each floor, with separate settings for each household. The town has 1,232 two-unit buildings, and the main limits are wall space, outdoor-unit location and the owner's approval.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Natick ranks sixth of 50 for electrically heated homes, with 3,202 of them, and only 16.6% of its units date from 2000 or later. We have not confirmed which utility serves each address, so the electric bill decides the rebate route.
body: ## Heat pumps in Natick: start with the bill

The 2026 Mass Save whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, and the house has to be weatherized first. We have not confirmed the utility for each Natick address, so your electric bill decides which route applies; the full terms are on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### The fuel counts
- Utility gas: 8,033 homes (51.6%).
- Fuel oil or kerosene: 3,787 homes (24.3%).
- Electricity: 3,202 homes (20.6%), sixth highest of the 50 towns.
- Bottled gas: 462 homes (3.0%).

Electric households can often swap resistance heat for a unit that moves heat instead of making it. Oil and bottled-gas homes buy fuel by delivery, so replacing some or all of that with electricity changes how the household budgets. Gas homes are the usual candidates for a partial setup, with the furnace kept for the coldest days.
### Age bands against the weatherization test

Only 2,657 units (16.6%) were built in 2000 or later. The 9,809 built before 1980 (61.3%) include 3,810 from 1940 to 1959 and 3,260 from 1939 or earlier, and for these the assessment step usually comes first. The 3,537 units from 1980 to 1999 miss the shortcut too, though they are likelier to be better sealed.
### Which kind of system

Detached houses are 9,063 units. Where ducts are sound, a ducted heat pump can replace a furnace, and where heat comes from radiators or baseboard, ductless heads avoid duct work. The 606 townhouse-style units and 1,232 two-family buildings often work out as one outdoor unit per household.
### Condos and converted buildings

With 6,332 units in multi-unit buildings, outdoor-unit approval is the first hurdle for many owners. Converted buildings such as the baseball factory condominiums of 1988 can have thick walls, and a ductless line set can often go through them with a small opening.
### High-value homes

At a median owner-occupied value of $710,100, many owners ask whether one system can do both seasons. A properly sized heat pump can, if the house is tight enough, and we assess the heating load before quoting.

faq.q: Which rebate applies to my Natick home?
faq.a: That depends on the electric utility serving your address and, for municipal utilities, on your heating fuel. Check your electric bill, then masssave.com or the utility. We have not confirmed the utility for each Natick address, and terms can change.

faq.q: Can a heat pump work in a Natick condo?
faq.a: Often, with association approval. Ductless systems need only a small wall opening, and outdoor unit placement is the main design question. Natick has 4,321 units in buildings of five or more, so it helps to raise the idea with the board early.

faq.q: Is a heat pump enough for a Massachusetts winter?
faq.a: Cold-climate models are built for it. In a tight, correctly sized house a heat pump can carry most of the season. In a leaky older house the old boiler may stay as backup. Natick's median home dates to 1966, so the second case is common.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Natick's oil homes need yearly burner cleaning, shared buildings benefit from coordinated service, and rental boilers are best checked before October. Maintenance is mostly about avoiding the cold-night call.
body: ## Tune-ups for a mixed-building town

Natick's housing runs from detached houses to condos and apartment buildings, so maintenance has several faces. A single owner schedules a visit. A condo board may need a contract. A landlord needs the boiler checked before the heating season.
### Oil, gas and electric

The 3,787 oil households need their burner cleaned every year, with a filter and nozzle change and a combustion test. The 8,033 gas homes get a safety inspection of the burner, heat exchanger, venting and controls. The 3,202 electric homes need coil, filter and refrigerant-side checks if they have heat pumps.
### Condo boards and landlords

A shared boiler is a single point of failure for many households. Regular service and written records help a board plan replacement. With 4,978 renter households, a lot of Natick equipment is run by someone other than the person who lives with it.
### Older equipment
The median Natick home dates to 1966, and 61.3% of units predate 1980. Older systems are worth a yearly look, since it tells you how much life is left.
### Seasonal calendar
- **Before the first frost:** furnace and boiler service.
- **Before the first heat wave:** air conditioner and mini-split checks.
- **Whenever something changes:** noises, smells, short cycling or a jump in your bill.
### Homeowner checklist
Replace filters on schedule, keep clear space around equipment, keep outdoor units free of leaves and snow, and check thermostat batteries. These habits head off many calls.
### What a visit includes

On a visit the technician goes over the heating or cooling unit, its controls and its electrical connections, then explains the findings plainly. If anything is wearing out, you get a written estimate before work starts.
### Equipment from 1980 to 1999
Natick has 3,537 units from 1980 to 1999 (22.1%). Original equipment in those homes has had a long run, and a check lets an owner plan the replacement instead of being surprised by it.
### Converted buildings
Equipment in converted factory buildings often sits in tight spaces. Access is part of the service plan, and the board should know where each unit is before the first visit.

faq.q: How often should I service an oil boiler in Natick?
faq.a: One visit a year, ahead of the heating season. It keeps soot down and helps avoid breakdowns. About 24.3% of Natick homes burn oil, so this is the second most common service group after gas, and the visit is also a chance to ask about the tank.

faq.q: Can a condo board arrange yearly service?
faq.a: Yes. A scheduled visit for shared equipment, with written findings, helps plan repairs and replacement. In a town where 39.6% of homes share a building, a service history is useful when the board compares repair costs with a replacement.

faq.q: Do newer Natick condos still need maintenance?
faq.a: Yes. Natick has 2,657 units from 2000 or later. Filters, coils and combustion settings drift in any system, and a young unit is easiest to keep in shape. A yearly visit also records the baseline for later comparison.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Natick has 20.4% of its homes from 1939 or earlier and 8.9% built since 2010, and 39.6% of homes share a building with others. Old buildings and new ones have different air problems, so we start with the building.
body: ## Air quality across old and new buildings
Natick's buildings span more than a century of construction, so indoor air problems vary. The first step is understanding how air and moisture move in your particular building.
### Older buildings

The town has 3,260 units from 1939 or earlier and another 3,810 from 1940 to 1959. Buildings of that age often have gaps around windows and chimneys that let dust, pollen and damp air in. If you plan renovation, a qualified specialist should test for older materials before work begins.
### Newer, tighter buildings
Natick has 2,657 units from 2000 or later, and 1,418 since 2010. Newer homes and condos are usually tighter, which saves energy but traps moisture and cooking fumes unless ventilation does its job.
### Shared buildings

In apartments and condos, air moves between units through shared walls, hallways and chases. Cooking smells, smoke and cleaning products can travel. With 6,332 units in multi-unit buildings, this is a regular complaint. Sealing gaps and exhaust fans that vent outside help.
### Converted factories

Condos in converted factories, such as the 1988 baseball factory conversion, can have tall rooms and thick walls. Air tends to stratify in tall rooms, so ceiling fans and well-placed returns matter there.
### Water nearby

Lake Cochituate and Dug Pond make up 7.04% of the town. If a basement near water smells musty, treat it as a moisture problem and find the source first. A dehumidifier lowers humidity but does not fix a leak.
### Filters and humidity
Better filters help when the blower can handle them. Indoor humidity swings affect wood floors and plaster as well as comfort, so a hygrometer is a cheap way to see what the air is doing.
### Ducts
Cleaning ducts is a job for visible dirt, mold or damage. It is not a yearly chore.
### What we can set up
- Better filtration and a change schedule.
- Humidifiers and dehumidifiers tied to the system.
- Ventilation for tight homes.
For regular checks see the [maintenance page](/cities/natick/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups).

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. If you can see dirt, mold or damage, or you have finished a renovation, it may help. Otherwise the gain is small. We look first and tell you what we find, including when the answer is that cleaning would not help.

faq.q: Does a tight new condo need ventilation?
faq.a: It can. Tight homes hold moisture and fumes, so fresh-air ventilation and good exhaust fans help. Natick has 2,657 units from 2000 or later, so this applies to a real slice of the town, especially where kitchens and baths are small.

faq.q: I live in a Natick apartment and smell my neighbor's cooking. What can I do?
faq.a: Run your kitchen and bath fans, seal visible gaps around pipes and outlets on shared walls, and use a portable filter. Anything in shared ducts or hallways needs the landlord or the board, since Natick has 6,332 units in multi-unit buildings.
